title: Introduce credential debouncer and stream iterator smoothing
author: Sofia Nguyen
release_notes: Adds a credential debouncer to reduce token refresh storms; smooths cross-SDK streaming iterators and backpressure hints; bumps SDK minor versions (py 1.9.0, ts 1.27.0, go 1.8.1). Opt-in behavior behind client config. No breaking changes to stable APIs.
description:
Context & motivation: In high-throughput streaming scenarios we observed correlated token refresh storms from multiple clients/hosts which amplify latency and cause transient 401 cascades. Simultaneously, SDK consumers reported awkward reconnect behavior and jitter when an auth refresh happened mid-iterator. This PR introduces a small, conservative "credential debouncer" (quiet window + suppression metric) that reduces refresh churn and pairs it with iterator smoothing hooks in all three SDKs to make reconnects and resume behaviour ergonomics-friendly.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a debouncer that: (1) detects and suppresses back-to-back refresh attempts within a configurable quiet window, (2) exposes lightweight telemetry for suppressed refreshes, (3) surfaces per-client and global toggles. SDK updates add iterator smoothing that buffers a minimal resume window to avoid noisy reconnects when a transient auth rotation occurs. Also standardizes retry preset names (latency-aware, conservative, throughput) and aligns default retry/backoff across Python/TS/Go.

Cross-SDK changes: Python: new auth.debouncer module, client-level config, unit + integration tests, bump to 1.9.0. TypeScript: stream iterator smoothing utility, auth adapter with quietWindow option, examples and docs, bump to 1.27.0. Go: token quiet-window implementation and iterator adapter, small API sugar to opt into smoothing, bump to 1.8.1. Core repo: small shim to surface debouncer telemetry to the Console and an example canary policy. Docs: added migration guidance and examples under docs/sdk/migration/credential-debouncer.md.

Testing & rollout: Unit tests added across all SDKs; end-to-end smoke and canary integration run in CI. Benchmarks show token-refresh storm suppression eliminates >70% of simultaneous refreshes in the synthetic workload; a memory micro-benchmark showed a ~3% regression in one TS allocation path (investigated and accepted as low-risk). Rollout plan: published packages to internal registry, canary 10% hosted traffic for 48h with telemetry thresholds; feature disabled by default for existing clients and enabled in new client templates.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative — quiet window defaults to 5s and suppression only postpones redundant refresh attempts (does not skip required expiry refreshes). Operator toggles are available in SDK constructors and via env vars for Private deployments.
